items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to updating and
modifying the tax abatements for certain solar and electric storage systems
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6640

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to updating and
modifying the tax abatements for certain solar and electric storage
systems

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To extend and enhance the solar electric generating system and electric
storage system tax abatements for New York City and provide for a tax
credit for the installation of such systems by non-profit owned and/or
income restricted affordable housing properties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill clarifies that the tax abatement for solar elec-
tric generating systems and electric energy storage equipment can be
used in conjunction. It defines eligible expenditures as reasonable
expenditures for materials, labor costs properly allocable to on-site
preparation, assembly, original installation, architectural and engi-
neering services, and designs and plans directly related to construction
or installation and adds solar parking canopy structures as an eligible
system.

Section two of the bill extends the period of the abatement for both
solar and electric energy storage systems to 2035 and sets the terms of
each abatement as the lesser of thirty percent of expenditures or
$250,000 taken in equal increments annually over a four-year period.
Properties that are owned by not-for-profit entities and/or income
restricted affordable housing properties would be eligible to receive a
direct-pay credit equal to the abatement through a check issued by the
New York City Department of Finance.

Section three of the bill includes conforming language extending the
abatement program to 2035.

Section four of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would extend and strengthen the existing incentive
programs passed by the legislature and signed into law by the Governor
to encourage the installation of solar electric generating systems and
energy storage systems, in connection with class one, class two and
class four properties in New York City. The program, while enabled by
the State, is administered and paid for by the City.  By extending the
period for when properties can apply for the abatement to 2035 and
allowing both types of abatements to be used together it will better
align with federal incentives from the Inflation Reduction Act, allowing
for the leveraging of federal dollars.

This legislation is also consistent with the commitments of New York
State in the Climate Leadership in the Climate Leadership and Community
Protection Act (CLCPA) and the City of New York through Local Law 97 to
reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to provide cleaner, more reliable
power for every New Yorker. It also now makes the incentives available
to not-for-profit owned properties such as houses of worship and income
restricted affordable properties through a direct credit provision,
thereby helping to meet environmental justice and equity goals. Contin-
uation and enhancement of the property tax abatement / credit is neces-
sary to offset a portion of the extra costs associated with NYC solar
energy installation, thus further stimulating clean energy investment
and job creation throughout New York City.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
